title: A Survey on Diffusion Language Models
caption: This comprehensive survey marks a pivotal moment for non-autoregressive models, consolidating the rapid progress of Diffusion Language Models (DLMs). It signals a major strategic shift in the field towards architectures that promise to solve the inference latency bottleneck of dominant autoregressive models, offering a future where parallel generation and fine-grained control become viable at scale.

title: We-Math 2.0: A Versatile MathBook System for Incentivizing Visual Mathematical Reasoning
caption: This paper represents the frontier of multimodal AI, moving beyond simple description to tackle complex, structured reasoning. By creating a complete, curriculum-based ecosystem for teaching visual math, it demonstrates a path towards building MLLMs that can solve formal problems, a critical step for scientific and engineering applications.

title: ScreenCoder: Advancing Visual-to-Code Generation for Front-End Automation via Modular Multimodal Agents
caption: A landmark paper in applied multimodal AI, ScreenCoder showcases a highly effective modular approach to a complex generation task. Its success suggests that for sophisticated, real-world problems, engineering interpretable, multi-agent systems around LLMs is a more robust strategy than relying on monolithic, black-box models.

title: The Knowledge-Reasoning Dissociation: Fundamental Limitations of LLMs in Clinical Natural Language Inference
caption: This critical work challenges the 'scaling is all you need' hypothesis by demonstrating a fundamental gap between knowing and reasoning in LLMs. Its findings have profound implications for the trustworthiness and near-term viability of deploying AI in high-stakes, regulated fields like medicine, forcing a necessary reckoning with the current limitations of the technology.

title: Reinforced Language Models for Sequential Decision Making
caption: This paper marks a key advance in creating autonomous AI agents by introducing a training algorithm specifically designed for long-horizon tasks. By showing that a smaller, intelligently trained 3B model can outperform a 72B baseline, it provides a crucial pathway for developing capable and efficient agents without relying on prohibitively large models.

title: Performance of GPT-5 in Brain Tumor MRI Reasoning
caption: Serving as an early and important reality check, this paper provides a sober, data-driven assessment of the new GPT-5's capabilities in a demanding, real-world domain. The finding that its performance is still not clinically viable underscores the persistent gap between general-purpose AI and reliable, specialist-level expertise, validating the need for domain-specific models and more fundamental research.
